scale_definition: 1 = peace. 5 = active gray-zone/hybrid conflict. 10 = open Russia-NATO/EU war. Use index_anchors for the level in between - each band names the observable condition that must be met.
credibility_scale: 1 = unverified/single unreliable source. 10 = confirmed by 10+ independent outlets.

tiers.name: Tier 3 - Interested-Party Press
tiers.note: flag for bias, cross-check against Tier 1/2

tiers.name: Excluded - Russian State Media & Unverified Accounts
tiers.note: never enters the credibility-weighted evidence base; tracked separately for narrative-pattern purposes only

byline_scoring_rules.principle: Evidence-only. Every score change must cite what it is based on. No subjective 'seems truthful' judgments.
signals: correction formally attached to this byline (negative, but transparency-partial-credit if self-initiated quickly)
claims later contradicted by independent Tier 1/2 reporting without the author correcting (negative, no partial credit)
claims confirmed by subsequent independent reporting (positive)

outlet_transparency_rules.principle: Separate from the static tier score. Tracks how an outlet handles being wrong.
signals: prompt, visible correction issued -> transparency score up
silent edit with no correction note -> transparency score down
claim contradicted by others and left uncorrected -> transparency score down

index_anchors.1: Peace. Normal diplomatic and economic relations; no coercive activity.
index_anchors.2: Friction. Hostile rhetoric and routine espionage; no operations against NATO/EU targets.
index_anchors.3: Political warfare. Sustained disinformation and election interference; no physical effects.
index_anchors.4: Gray-zone pressure. Deniable sabotage, GPS jamming, airspace probing; no casualties on NATO/EU soil.
index_anchors.5: Active hybrid conflict. State-directed sabotage on NATO/EU soil attributed by governments; proxy war ongoing.
index_anchors.6: Intensified hybrid. NATO members respond militarily (interceptions, shootdowns); attributed sabotage with casualty risk; force posture changes.
index_anchors.7: Pre-crisis. Article 4 consultations, or kinetic incidents on NATO territory without fatalities; visible reinforcement.
index_anchors.8: Crisis. Fatalities on NATO/EU territory from Russian action, or direct limited fire exchange between Russian and NATO forces.
index_anchors.9: Brink. Sustained direct military exchange between Russia and a NATO member; Article 5 under active consideration.

index_scoring_note: Score the Russia-NATO/EU relationship, not the intensity of the war in Ukraine. Severe fighting inside Ukraine does not by itself raise this index above 5-6; what moves it is what happens to NATO/EU members and forces. The index must be able to fall: if the evidence for a previous level has weakened, say so and lower it.
